problem_type: MCP catalog source changes are invisible to connected clients
symptom: A connected MCP client cannot know that the playbook or capability projection catalog changed because initialize advertises no tools/list_changed support and no server notification is emitted.
direct_cause: The protocol hardcodes an empty tools capability and the catalog source registration paths have no shared change-notification boundary.
class_root: MCP catalog source registrations do not converge on a session-aware notification bus.
affected_population: Playbook and explicit MCP capability adapter registrations
internal_only_reason: The notification bus and CI ownership are Nomi's internal transport contract; the protocol method name is directly exercised by the L1 contract.
invariants: Every accepted catalog source registration emits one shared change event.
stdio session teardown unsubscribes the listener.
generality_proof: Playbook and capability projection registrations are the two current catalog source paths identified by the five-way mcpToolCatalog assembly; both call the same emitter, and every protocol session subscribes through createMcpProtocol.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Fan out the single catalog-change event to active sessions.
Gate catalog notifications on successful initialize and dispose the subscription.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: A newly validated playbook emits through the shared catalog-change boundary.
Explicit capability adapter resolver registration emits through the same boundary.
The journey is attached to the existing journeys risk surface rather than creating a second classifier.

recurrence.reason: Future catalog sources can otherwise register successfully while every already connected host remains on a stale tools/list view.
same_class_scan: Checked both source registration paths and the protocol/session teardown path.

prevention.invariant: All catalog source changes fan out to initialized protocol sessions as notifications/tools/list_changed.
prevention.failure_mode: A stale session is observable by the L1 test and the registration path cannot silently bypass the shared emitter.
prevention.strategy: Use one small process-local event bus and a session lifecycle subscription; do not duplicate source-specific notification logic in the protocol.

legacy_paths.rationale: No prior notification path existed; the empty capabilities declaration is replaced in place and no fallback is retained.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant is internal to Nomi's hand-written MCP protocol and registry lifecycle.

migration: No persisted state changes; existing clients simply re-list after the standard notification.
residual_risks: The current catalog remains explicit and 42-tool scoped; future source registration must continue to use the validated registration paths.
